title: Kirchberg's embedding problem
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's negative answer (2026) to Kirchberg's embedding problem: the full C*-algebra of the group Z[1/2]^3 semidirect (SL_3(Z) x Z) has no unital embedding into the norm ultrapower of any nuclear unital C*-algebra, in particular not into the ultrapower of the Cuntz algebra O_2. The proof is given in full from two named hypotheses: property (T) of the group Z^3 semidirect SL_3(Z), and, for the specialization to O_2, the nuclearity of O_2. The first lesson collects the facts on C*-algebras that are used, introduces norm ultrapowers and full group C*-algebras, states the theorem and studies the group. The second lesson defines a spectral test for the occurrence of a finite-dimensional representation in a tuple of unitaries and proves that in a nuclear C*-algebra only finitely many irreducible representations pass the test. The third lesson proves the theorem: an embedding would give finite sets of representations in which every member has a predecessor under an endomorphism of index eight, and finite chains of predecessors force a periodicity that the group excludes.
prerequisites: course Foundations of von Neumann algebras: C*-algebras, the continuous functional calculus, positivity, quotients, injective *-homomorphisms, spectral permanence (lesson Order, local units and quotients of C*-algebras); faithful representations (lesson Building representations from positive functionals); Hilbert tensor products and compact operators; trace-class and Hilbert-Schmidt operators
course Positive maps and finite-dimensional approximation (OA-APPROX), lesson Tensor positivity and nuclearity: the minimal and the maximal tensor product and nuclearity as their equality
unitary representations of groups of finite dimension (defined in the lessons)
the lessons prove every other fact they use, except the named hypotheses (T) and (O) of the first lesson and the quoted consequences in the last section of the third lesson

checks.reading: The manuscript 'An explicit obstruction to nuclear norm-ultrapower embeddings' (OpenAI, 23 Sep 2026, in the revision of the repository on 13 Oct 2026; six sections, one figure, 1,055 lines of TeX) was read in full on 13 Oct 2026, and every step of its argument was derived again while the lessons were written: the group law, the conjugation by t, the cosets of the image of theta; the representation pi_*; the Laplacian and its spectral gap; the correspondence of invariant vectors and intertwiners; the square-root trace inequality with its trace manipulations; the density operator argument and the constant kappa^2/(4|S|); the absence of finite-dimensional parts in the sequence algebra; the passage through the minimal and the maximal tensor product; the functional calculus argument; unitary lifts; the gap for varying dimensions; the induced representation of pi_* and the use of injectivity; the transport by x_n(t); the induction with eight cosets and the estimate of the components; the reciprocity argument; the chain lemma. No error found. Differences of presentation, none a correction: conjugate representations are written with conjugate matrices and maps T_xi in place of conjugate Hilbert spaces; the passage from generators to all group elements is done with the subgroup of the elements for which the vectors are almost invariant, in place of an argument with fixed words; property (T) is used in the form of a Kazhdan pair, and its equivalence with the usual definition for countable groups is an exercise with solution; the proof that elementary matrices generate SL_3(Z) is written out; an explicit pi_* of dimension 7 is given. Observations added, each with its proof or as an exercise with solution: the proof uses only that G contains a finitely generated subgroup with property (T), an element conjugating it onto a subgroup of finite index, and a finite-dimensional irreducible representation that is not periodic under this conjugation; the proof covers ultraproducts of varying nuclear unital algebras; the representation pi_7 is a predecessor of the trivial representation. The proofs in these papers were not read. The theorems of Goldbring and Sinclair behind the three quoted consequences were not checked. The nuclearity of O_2 is quoted. open_obligations: Named hypothesis (T): the group Z^3 semidirect SL_3(Z) has property (T) (de Cornulier, arXiv:math/0502140, Proposition 1.1 with n = 3, m = 1). It is not proved in the programme. The whole theorem depends on it.

Named hypothesis (O): the Cuntz algebra O_2 is nuclear (Cuntz). It is not proved in the programme. Only the specialization to Kirchberg's embedding problem (Corollary 4.2 of the first lesson) depends on it.

The three consequences in Section 8 of the third lesson (existential closure, crossed products, good nuclear witnesses) are quoted from the manuscript, which derives them from theorems of Goldbring and Sinclair; they are not proved in the programme and the cited theorems were not checked.

The programme results on C*-algebras, trace-class operators and tensor norms that are used are cited with their numbers; their proofs were not checked again for this course. The lesson on tensor norms is by another author of the programme (GPT-6.1 Sol).

Not in the course: the theorem of Kirchberg and Phillips on exact algebras; the equivalence of the unital and the nonunital form of the embedding problem (Exercise 9.5 of the third lesson treats a special case).
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
